```{r}
#| include: false
# The per-cell summary of the maximal grid: one row for each estimand cell that
# the six Level 1 choices define, with the number of measurement and estimation
# variants fitted inside it and where their claim-aligned partial correlations
# sit. Written by the article repository's R/17 alongside the shards under
# data/grid/, which this page fetches one at a time. This page is the ring
# version of estimand-dial.qmd: the same main panel, driven by three dials in
# the sidebar instead of fourteen selects.
cells <- read.csv("../data/grid/cells_summary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ojs_define(cells_raw = cells)
```

## {.sidebar width="500px"}

<span class="lv lv1">Level 1 – Estimands</span>
<p class="lv-note">Each ring is one choice that rewrites the estimand statement, and the option under the red index at twelve o'clock is the one chosen. Click any segment and its ring turns to bring it under the index. From the outside in: four rings that name the variables – the outcome twice, which frames and how they are scored – two that say whom the question is about, and the estimator, which says how they are compared.</p>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dial1_input = ringDial({
  size: 470, ringW: 22, gapIn: 2, gapOut: 8, fontSize: 9, nameSize: 7,
  centre: ["Level 1", "the question"],
  value: {outcome: "mcosmo", construction: "share", predictor: "unemp", copredictor: "none", sample: "all", reg_weight: "none", estimator: "fe_twoway"},
  rings: rings1
})
```

<p class="dial-legend"><span style="background:#0e3b6a"></span>the variables (frames, scoring, predictor, adjustment) &nbsp;&nbsp; <span style="background:#0f6b6b"></span>whom it is about &nbsp;&nbsp; <span style="background:#8c5a10"></span>how they are compared</p>

<span class="lv lv2">Level 2 – Measurement</span>
<p class="lv-note">The same question, put to the data differently. The statement does not change; the answer may. The outer three rings build the outcome; the inner ring names the published series behind the predictor, and it offers the growth series once the predictor ring is turned to GDP growth.</p>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dial2_input = ringDial({
  size: 400, ringW: 24, gapIn: 2, gapOut: 8, fontSize: 9.5, nameSize: 7.5,
  centre: ["Level 2", "the measurement"],
  value: {noop: "zero", item_set: "all", cell_weight: "unweighted", measure: "wb_nat"},
  rings: rings2("unemp")
})
```

<span class="lv lv3">Level 3 – Estimation</span>
<p class="lv-note">Neither the question nor the measures change; only the fitting does.</p>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dial3_input = ringDial({
  size: 300, ringW: 24, gapIn: 2, gapOut: 8, fontSize: 9.5, nameSize: 7.5,
  centre: ["Level 3", "the arithmetic"],
  value: {pred_form: "raw", family: "gaussian", se: "conventional"},
  rings: rings3
})
```

<p class="lv-note" style="margin-top:0.9rem">The rings open on C6HJR's published Multi100 specification. Nothing is fitted in the browser: every number is read from the pre-computed grid, one small file per question.</p>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Everything behind the dials. This chunk displays nothing: a named cell whose
// value is not a DOM node would otherwise print as an inspector line wherever
// the chunk sits. The dials themselves are created in the visible chunks
// above, because a node first attached inside a hidden chunk is never moved.

// A watch-style dial: one ring per choice, from the outside in, each divided
// into its options. The option under the red index at twelve o'clock is the
// one chosen. Click a segment and its ring turns, the short way round, until
// that segment is under the index. Rings of one cluster sit close together
// and a wider gap separates the clusters; the ring names stand on white
// pills at nine o'clock and do not turn. The element carries `value` (an
// object of the settings) and fires `input`, so Generators.input reads it;
// `setLevels(key, levels, value)` rebuilds one ring with new options and
// `setCentre(a, b, c)` writes up to three lines in the centre disc.
ringDial = ({rings, value, size = 560, ringW = 26, gapIn = 3, gapOut = 11, fontSize = 11, nameSize = 8.5, margin = 10, centre = null}) => {
  const c = size / 2, outerR = c - margin;
  const state = {...value}, theta = {}, groups = {};
  const el = document.createElement("div");
  el.className = "dial";
  el.style.cssText = `display:block;width:100%;max-width:${size}px;margin:0 auto`;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${size} ${size}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("display", "block").style("font-family", "system-ui, sans-serif");
  const rad = d => d * Math.PI / 180;
  // ring radii from the outside in, a wider gap between clusters
  const radii = [];
  let edge = outerR;
  rings.forEach((rg, i) => {
    if (i > 0) edge -= rings[i - 1].cluster === rg.cluster ? gapIn : gapOut;
    radii.push([edge - ringW, edge]);
    edge -= ringW;
  });
  const innerR = edge;
  const ringsLayer = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${c},${c})`);
  const namesLayer = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${c},${c})`).style("pointer-events", "none");
  function build(rg, i) {
    const [r0, r1] = radii[i], rm = (r0 + r1) / 2, n = rg.levels.length, seg = 360 / n;
    if (groups[rg.key]) groups[rg.key].remove();
    const g = ringsLayer.append("g");
    groups[rg.key] = g;
    const idx0 = Math.max(0, rg.levels.findIndex(l => l.value === state[rg.key]));
    state[rg.key] = rg.levels[idx0].value;
    theta[rg.key] = -(idx0 * seg + seg / 2);
    const arc = d3.arc().innerRadius(r0).outerRadius(r1).padAngle(0.014).padRadius(r1);
    const data = rg.levels.map((l, j) => ({...l, j}));
    const segs = g.selectAll("path").data(data).join("path")
      .attr("stroke", rg.colour).attr("stroke-width", 1.2).style("cursor", "pointer");
    segs.append("title").text(d => `${rg.label}: ${d.label}`);
    const labels = g.selectAll("text").data(data).join("text")
      .attr("font-size", fontSize).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("dominant-baseline", "middle")
      .style("pointer-events", "none").text(d => d.label);
    const pillHalf = (rg.label.length * nameSize * 0.66 + 10) / 2;
    const paint = () => {
      segs.attr("fill", d => d.value === state[rg.key] ? rg.colour : "#fff");
      labels.attr("fill", d => d.value === state[rg.key] ? "#fff" : "#111f2c")
        .attr("font-weight", d => d.value === state[rg.key] ? 600 : 400);
    };
    const draw = () => {
      const t = theta[rg.key];
      segs.attr("d", d => arc({startAngle: rad(d.j * seg + t), endAngle: rad((d.j + 1) * seg + t)}));
      labels.attr("transform", d => {
        const deg = (d.j + 0.5) * seg + t, a = rad(deg);
        const abs = ((deg % 360) + 360) % 360, flip = abs > 90 && abs < 270;
        return `translate(${rm * Math.sin(a)},${-rm * Math.cos(a)}) rotate(${deg + (flip ? 180 : 0)})`;
      })
        // a label passing under the ring's name at nine o'clock fades out
        .attr("opacity", d => {
          const abs = (((d.j + 0.5) * seg + t) % 360 + 360) % 360;
          const dist = Math.min(Math.abs(abs - 270), 360 - Math.abs(abs - 270));
          const span = (d.label.length * fontSize * 0.27 + pillHalf + 3) / rm * 180 / Math.PI;
          return dist < span ? 0.12 : 1;
        });
    };
    paint(); draw();
    segs.on("click", (event, d) => {
      const target = -(d.j * seg + seg / 2), from = theta[rg.key];
      const delta = ((target - from) % 360 + 540) % 360 - 180;
      g.transition().duration(520).ease(d3.easeCubicInOut)
        .tween("turn", () => { const ip = d3.interpolateNumber(from, from + delta); return t => { theta[rg.key] = ip(t); draw(); }; })
        .on("end", () => { theta[rg.key] = target; draw(); });
      state[rg.key] = d.value;
      paint();
      el.value = {...state};
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
    });
  }
  rings.forEach(build);
  // the ring names, on white pills at nine o'clock, drawn above the rings
  rings.forEach((rg, i) => {
    const rm = (radii[i][0] + radii[i][1]) / 2, label = rg.label.toUpperCase(), w = label.length * nameSize * 0.66 + 10;
    const g = namesLayer.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${-rm},0) rotate(-90)`);
    g.append("rect").attr("x", -w / 2).attr("y", -nameSize * 0.8).attr("width", w).attr("height", nameSize * 1.6)
      .attr("rx", nameSize * 0.8).attr("fill", "#fff").attr("fill-opacity", 0.92);
    g.append("text").attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("dominant-baseline", "middle").attr("font-size", nameSize)
      .attr("font-weight", 700).attr("letter-spacing", "0.06em").attr("fill", rg.colour).text(label);
  });
  // the index: a red marker above the outer ring and a hairline down to the centre disc
  svg.append("path").attr("d", `M ${c - 8} ${margin - 9} L ${c + 8} ${margin - 9} L ${c} ${margin + 2} Z`).attr("fill", "#96131b");
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", c).attr("y1", margin + 2).attr("x2", c).attr("y2", c - innerR).attr("stroke", "#96131b")
    .attr("stroke-width", 1.5).attr("stroke-dasharray", "2,3").style("pointer-events", "none");
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", c).attr("cy", c).attr("r", Math.max(innerR - 3, 4)).attr("fill", "#f4f6f8").attr("stroke", "#d6dde5");
  const fBig = Math.min(16, innerR * 0.42), fSmall = Math.min(10, innerR * 0.28);
  const big = svg.append("text").attr("x", c).attr("y", c - 2).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", fBig).attr("font-weight", 600).attr("fill", "#111f2c");
  const small = svg.append("text").attr("x", c).attr("y", c + fSmall * 1.5).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", fSmall).attr("fill", "#3c4a56");
  const small2 = svg.append("text").attr("x", c).attr("y", c + fSmall * 2.8).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", fSmall).attr("fill", "#3c4a56");
  el.setCentre = (a, b, d) => { big.text(a ?? ""); small.text(b ?? ""); small2.text(d ?? ""); };
  if (centre) el.setCentre(...centre);
  el.setLevels = (key, levels, value) => {
    const i = rings.findIndex(r => r.key === key);
    if (i < 0) return;
    rings[i].levels = levels;
    state[key] = levels.some(l => l.value === value) ? value : levels[0].value;
    build(rings[i], i);
    el.value = {...state};
  };
  el.value = {...state};
  el.append(svg.node());
  return el;
}

// The six Level 1 choices in the order the choices page uses: the variables in
// blues, whom the question is about in teals, how they are compared in bronze.
palette1 = {
  return {outcome: "#0e3b6a", construction: "#1f4c7c", predictor: "#35659a", copredictor: "#5484b3", sample: "#0f6b6b", reg_weight: "#2b8585", estimator: "#8c5a10"};
}
rings1 = [
  {key: "outcome", label: "Frames", cluster: "variables", colour: palette1.outcome, levels: [{label: "cosmopolitan", value: "mcosmo"}, {label: "utilitarian", value: "mutil"}, {label: "all positive", value: "mpos"}, {label: "communitarian", value: "mcomm"}, {label: "libertarian", value: "mlib"}, {label: "all negative", value: "mneg"}]},
  {key: "construction", label: "Scored as", cluster: "variables", colour: palette1.construction, levels: [{label: "share of mentions", value: "share"}, {label: "count of items", value: "count"}, {label: "count per item", value: "rate"}]},
  {key: "predictor", label: "Predictor", cluster: "variables", colour: palette1.predictor, levels: [{label: "unemployment", value: "unemp"}, {label: "GDP growth", value: "growth"}]},
  {key: "copredictor", label: "Adjusted for", cluster: "variables", colour: palette1.copredictor, levels: [{label: "nothing", value: "none"}, {label: "the other measure", value: "other"}]},
  {key: "sample", label: "Sample", cluster: "population", colour: palette1.sample, levels: [{label: "all years", value: "all"}, {label: "2004–2008", value: "y2004_2008"}, {label: "2009–2013", value: "y2009_2013"}, {label: "no bailout states", value: "no_bailout"}, {label: "no GR, ES", value: "no_GR_ES"}]},
  {key: "reg_weight", label: "Weight", cluster: "population", colour: palette1.reg_weight, levels: [{label: "none", value: "none"}, {label: "respondents", value: "n_cell"}, {label: "effective n", value: "n_eff"}, {label: "population", value: "pop"}]},
  {key: "estimator", label: "Estimator", cluster: "method", colour: palette1.estimator, levels: [{label: "two-way FE", value: "fe_twoway"}, {label: "country FE", value: "fe_country"}, {label: "random effects", value: "re"}, {label: "pooled OLS", value: "pooled_cl"}]}
]
// the published series behind each predictor: five for unemployment, two for growth
unempSeries = [{label: "WB national", value: "wb_nat"}, {label: "ES 15–74 active", value: "es_1574_act"}, {label: "ES 20–64 pop.", value: "es_2064_pop"}, {label: "ES 25–64 LFS", value: "es_2564_lfs"}, {label: "ES 15–74 tips", value: "es_1574_tips"}]
growthSeries = [{label: "WB growth", value: "wb_growth"}, {label: "ES growth", value: "es_growth"}]
// Level 2 in greens: four rings that build the outcome, then the series ring
rings2 = pred => [
  {key: "noop", label: "No opinion", cluster: "outcome", colour: "#3f6d35", levels: [{label: "scored zero", value: "zero"}, {label: "dropped", value: "drop"}, {label: "split", value: "split"}, {label: "imputed, mice", value: "mi_mice"}, {label: "imputed, Amelia", value: "mi_amelia"}]},
  {key: "item_set", label: "Items", cluster: "outcome", colour: "#4a7a3f", levels: [{label: "all 13 items", value: "all"}, {label: "without 'unemployment'", value: "un"}]},
  {key: "cell_weight", label: "Cell means", cluster: "outcome", colour: "#5a8a4e", levels: [{label: "as interviewed", value: "unweighted"}, {label: "design-weighted", value: "design"}]},
  {key: "measure", label: "Series", cluster: "predictor", colour: "#1f4d1b", levels: pred === "unemp" ? unempSeries : growthSeries}
]
// Level 3 in violets
rings3 = [
  {key: "pred_form", label: "Form", cluster: "fit", colour: "#5f4f78", levels: [{label: "raw", value: "raw"}, {label: "logged", value: "log"}]},
  {key: "family", label: "Family", cluster: "fit", colour: "#7b6a8f", levels: [{label: "linear", value: "gaussian"}, {label: "beta, logit link", value: "beta"}]},
  {key: "se", label: "Std errors", cluster: "fit", colour: "#8f7ea3", levels: [{label: "conventional", value: "conventional"}, {label: "clustered by country", value: "clustered"}]}
]

dialValue1 = Generators.input(dial1_input)
dialValue2 = Generators.input(dial2_input)
dialValue3 = Generators.input(dial3_input)
colourBy = Generators.input(colourBy_input)

// the fourteen choices under the names the main panel uses
outcome = dialValue1.outcome
predictor = dialValue1.predictor
copredictor = dialValue1.copredictor
sample = dialValue1.sample
weights = dialValue1.reg_weight
estimator = dialValue1.estimator
construction = dialValue1.construction
noop = dialValue2.noop
item_set = dialValue2.item_set
cell_weight = dialValue2.cell_weight
pred_form = dialValue3.pred_form
family = dialValue3.family
se = dialValue3.se
// the series ring is rebuilt whenever the predictor ring turns, so the value
// read here is guarded against the moment between the turn and the rebuild
measureSync = {
  const levels = predictor === "unemp" ? unempSeries : growthSeries;
  const keep = dial2_input.value.measure;
  dial2_input.setLevels("measure", levels, levels.some(l => l.value === keep) ? keep : levels[0].value);
  dial2_input.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
  return predictor;
}
measure = {
  measureSync;
  const m = dialValue2.measure;
  const ok = (predictor === "unemp" ? unempSeries : growthSeries).some(l => l.value === m);
  return ok ? m : (predictor === "unemp" ? "wb_nat" : "wb_growth");
}

cells = transpose(cells_raw)
cellKey = d => [d.outcome, d.predictor, d.copredictor, d.estimator, d.sample, d.reg_weight].join("__")
cellId = [outcome, predictor, copredictor, estimator, sample, weights].join("__")
cell = cells.find(d => cellKey(d) === cellId && d.construction === construction)
// the questions the menu can ask: the per-item rate repeats its count for the
// linear family, so it is not counted as a question of its own
questions = cells.filter(d => d.construction !== "rate")

// One shard per question, fetched when the Level 1 choices settle on it. The file
// is gzipped; the browser inflates it unless the server already did.
async function readCsvGz(url) {
  const res = await fetch(url);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`The results file for this question could not be fetched (${url}).`);
  const buf = await res.arrayBuffer();
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(buf);
  let text;
  if (bytes[0] === 0x1f && bytes[1] === 0x8b) {
    if (typeof DecompressionStream === "undefined")
      throw new Error("This browser cannot inflate the results file; a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari can.");
    const stream = new Blob([buf]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"));
    text = await new Response(stream).text();
  } else {
    text = new TextDecoder().decode(buf);
  }
  // R writes logicals as TRUE/FALSE, which autoType leaves as strings; NA stays a string too
  return d3.csvParse(text, d3.autoType).map(d => ({...d,
    sig: d.sig === true || d.sig === "TRUE",
    supports_claim: d.supports_claim === true || d.supports_claim === "TRUE"}));
}

shard = cell === undefined
  ? []
  // the file holds every scoring rule; the question is the rows under the chosen one
  : (await readCsvGz(`../data/grid/${cellId}.csv.gz`)).filter(d => d.construction === construction && typeof d.r_ca === "number" && Number.isFinite(d.r_ca))

within = ["construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form", "family", "se"]
// written as blocks with a return: Quarto's dashboard rewrite drops the
// parentheses of an object-literal cell, which would turn it into a block of
// bare statements with no value
current = { return {construction, noop, item_set, cell_weight, measure, pred_form, family, se}; }
hit = shard.find(d => within.every(k => String(d[k]) === String(current[k])))
curve = shard.slice().sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.r_ca, b.r_ca)).map((d, i) => ({...d, rank: i + 1, isCurrent: d === hit}))

axisLabel = {
  return {construction: "Outcome built as", noop: "No-opinion respondents", item_set: "Items", cell_weight: "Cell means",
          measure: "Published series", pred_form: "Predictor form", family: "Outcome family", se: "Standard errors"};
}
// a categorical palette written out, because the Plot build in the OJS runtime
// does not know the newer named schemes
palette = ["#4e79a7", "#f28e2b", "#e15759", "#76b7b2", "#59a14f", "#edc948", "#b07aa1", "#ff9da7", "#9c755f", "#bab0ac"]

// the frames each set names, the items in each set (all 13 items, or without the
// "unemployment" item, which leaves the communitarian set with three), and the
// number words the statement uses for the per-item rate
frameName = { return {mcosmo: "cosmopolitan", mutil: "utilitarian", mpos: "positive", mcomm: "communitarian", mlib: "libertarian", mneg: "negative"}; }
kItems = { return {all: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 4, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 6}, un: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 3, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 5}}; }
numWord = { return {2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven"}; }

labels = {
  return {
  // the frame set names the frames and the scoring rule says what "more" means
  outcome: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(frameName).map(([k, nm]) => [k,
    construction === "count" ? `the number of ${nm} frames people attach to the EU`
    : construction === "rate" ? `the proportion of the ${numWord[kItems[item_set][k]]} ${nm} frames that people attach to the EU`
    : `the share of ${nm} frames among the frames people attach to the EU`])),
  predictor: {unemp: "the national unemployment rate", growth: "national GDP growth"},
  units: {
    all:        "the 270 country-years of the 27 member states surveyed between 2004 and 2013",
    y2004_2008: "the country-years of 2004 to 2008, before the crisis",
    y2009_2013: "the country-years of 2009 to 2013, during and after it",
    no_bailout: "the country-years of the states that never entered an assistance programme",
    no_GR_ES:   "the country-years of every state other than Greece and Spain"
  },
  comparison: {
    fe_twoway:  "each country with itself over time, net of what all countries share in a given year",
    fe_country: "each country with itself over time",
    re:         "a blend of change within countries and differences between them, in proportion to how precisely each is measured",
    pooled_cl:  "country-years with one another as one pool, so that differences between countries carry the comparison"
  },
  weighting: {
    none:   "each country-year counting once",
    n_cell: "each country-year counting in proportion to the respondents behind its average",
    n_eff:  "each country-year counting in proportion to its effective sample size once the design weights are applied",
    pop:    "each country counting in proportion to its adult population, so that the answer describes people rather than country-years"
  },
  measured: {
    noop: {zero: "scoring respondents who named nothing as zero", drop: "leaving out respondents who named nothing",
           split: "splitting the share of respondents who named nothing evenly across the scales",
           mi_mice: "imputing the answers of respondents who named nothing (mice)",
           mi_amelia: "imputing the answers of respondents who named nothing (Amelia)"},
    item_set: {all: "from all 13 items", un: "from the 12 items other than 'unemployment'"},
    cell_weight: {unweighted: "with cells averaged as interviewed", design: "with design-weighted cells"},
    measure: {wb_nat: "the World Bank series", es_1574_act: "Eurostat's 15–74 rate as a share of the active population",
              es_2064_pop: "Eurostat's 20–64 rate as a share of the population", es_2564_lfs: "Eurostat's 25–64 labour-force-survey rate",
              es_1574_tips: "Eurostat's headline 15–74 table", wb_growth: "the World Bank growth series", es_growth: "Eurostat's growth series"}
  }
  };
}
adjustment = copredictor === "other"
  ? (predictor === "unemp" ? ", holding GDP growth fixed" : ", holding the unemployment rate fixed")
  : ""

fmt = d3.format(".3f")
problem = cell === undefined
  ? "That pairing is not in the universe: the random-effects estimator is never fitted with regression weights. Set the weight to none or choose another estimator."
  : hit === undefined
    ? (family === "beta" && construction === "count" ? "A count of items is not a proportion, so it has no beta twin. Choose the per-item rate, which is the count divided by the number of items in the set, or the linear family."
       : family === "beta" ? "The beta family was pre-computed only at the canonical measurement settings: the share or the per-item rate of all 13 items, no-opinion respondents scored zero, cells as interviewed, the World Bank series."
       : noop.startsWith("mi_") ? "The imputed options were pre-computed only for the unemployment arm at the canonical settings: share of all 13 items, cells as interviewed, World Bank series, raw form, linear family."
       : "That combination was not fitted.")
    : null
placement = hit === undefined ? NaN : d3.mean(questions, d => d.median_rca < hit.r_ca ? 1 : 0)
verdict = hit === undefined ? null
  : hit.supports_claim && hit.sig ? ["for", "supports the claim, p < .05"]
  : hit.supports_claim ? ["ns", "claim's direction, not significant"]
  : ["against", "against the claim's direction"]
statLabel = family === "beta" ? "z" : "t"

// The six Level 1 choices in the order of the rings, with the ring colours.
level1 = [
  {key: "outcome", label: "Frames", cluster: "variables", levels: {mcosmo: "cosmopolitan", mutil: "utilitarian", mpos: "all positive", mcomm: "communitarian", mlib: "libertarian", mneg: "all negative"}},
  {key: "construction", label: "Scored as", cluster: "variables", levels: {share: "share of mentions", count: "count of items", rate: "count per item"}},
  {key: "predictor", label: "Predictor", cluster: "variables", levels: {unemp: "unemployment", growth: "GDP growth"}},
  {key: "copredictor", label: "Adjusted for", cluster: "variables", levels: {none: "nothing", other: "the other measure"}},
  {key: "sample", label: "Sample", cluster: "population", levels: {all: "all years", y2004_2008: "2004–2008", y2009_2013: "2009–2013", no_bailout: "no bailout states", no_GR_ES: "no GR, ES"}},
  {key: "reg_weight", label: "Weight", cluster: "population", levels: {none: "none", n_cell: "respondents", n_eff: "effective n", pop: "population"}},
  {key: "estimator", label: "Estimator", cluster: "method", levels: {fe_twoway: "two-way FE", fe_country: "country FE", re: "random effects", pooled_cl: "pooled OLS"}}
]
clusterColour = { return {variables: "#0e3b6a", population: "#0f6b6b", method: "#8c5a10"}; }
now = { return {outcome, construction, predictor, copredictor, estimator, sample, reg_weight: weights}; }
neighbours = level1.flatMap(a =>
  Object.keys(a.levels).map(lv => {
    const c = cells.find(d => level1.every(b => b.key === a.key ? d[b.key] === lv : d[b.key] === now[b.key]));
    return {axis: a.label, cluster: a.cluster, row: `${a.label} · ${a.levels[lv]}`, median: c ? c.median_rca : null,
            lo: c ? c.min_rca : null, hi: c ? c.max_rca : null, share_sig: c ? c.share_sig : null,
            isCurrent: lv === now[a.key], exists: c !== undefined};
  }))
rows = neighbours.map(d => d.row)
band = shard.length > 0 ? [d3.quantile(shard, 0.1, d => d.r_ca), d3.quantile(shard, 0.9, d => d.r_ca)] : null
firstOfAxis = level1.map(a => neighbours.find(d => d.axis === a.label).row).slice(1)
```

## Column

### Row {.flow}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| title: "The estimand statement"
html`<p class="estimand">Among <b>${labels.units[sample]}</b>, the association between <b>${labels.predictor[predictor]}</b>
  <span class="measured">(measured as ${labels.measured.measure[measure]})</span> and <b>${labels.outcome[outcome]}</b>
  <span class="measured">(built ${labels.measured.item_set[item_set]}, ${labels.measured.noop[noop]}, ${labels.measured.cell_weight[cell_weight]})</span>,
  comparing <b>${labels.comparison[estimator]}</b>${adjustment}, with <b>${labels.weighting[weights]}</b>.</p>
<p class="small" style="margin-top:0.6rem">Blue is the question. Green is how it is measured: turn a ring of the Level 2 dial and only the green words move. The Level 3 dial changes nothing in the statement.</p>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| title: "The chosen specification"
problem !== null
  ? html`<p class="small" style="color:#96131b">${problem}</p>`
  : html`<span class="chip ${verdict[0]}">${verdict[1]}</span>
<div class="readout">
  <div><div class="k">Coefficient</div><div class="v">${d3.format(".5f")(hit.estimate)}</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">${statLabel} on ${Math.round(hit.df)} df</div><div class="v">${fmt(hit.statistic)}</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">p</div><div class="v">${hit.p < 0.001 ? "< 0.001" : fmt(hit.p)}</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">aligned r</div><div class="v">${fmt(hit.r_ca)}</div></div>
</div>
<p class="small">Without changing the question, the answer can be moved from <b>${fmt(d3.min(shard, d => d.r_ca))}</b> to <b>${fmt(d3.max(shard, d => d.r_ca))}</b> by the Level 2 and Level 3 choices alone (median ${fmt(d3.median(shard, d => d.r_ca))}; ${Math.round(100 * d3.mean(shard, d => d.sig ? 1 : 0))}% of the ${shard.length} answers significant). Among the ${questions.length.toLocaleString()} questions the menu can ask, ${Math.round(100 * placement)}% have a median answer more claim-supporting than this one.</p>`
```

                     fill: colourBy === "none" ? (d => d.sig ? "#0e3b6a" : "#b7c2cc") : colourBy,
                     title: d => `${d.construction}, ${d.noop}, items: ${d.item_set}, cells: ${d.cell_weight}, ${d.measure}\n${d.pred_form}, ${d.family}, se: ${d.se}\nr_ca = ${d.r_ca.toFixed(3)}${d.sig ? " (p < .05)" : ""}`}),
    Plot.dot(curve.filter(d => d.isCurrent), {x: "rank", y: "r_ca", r: 8, fill: "none", stroke: "#c77c00", strokeWidth: 2.5}),

  ]

<p class="caption">Each dot is one way of answering the question the Level 1 dial fixes: one combination of the Level 2 and Level 3 options, read from the pre-computed grid. Dark blue dots are significant at the five per cent level, grey ones are not. The orange ring is the chosen specification, and the dashed line is the question's median answer. Hover over a dot for its options. The menu above the chart colours the dots by one Level 2 or Level 3 choice, to show which of its options sit where along the curve.</p>

### Row {.tabset .flow}

::: {.card title="One ring at a time"}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  height: 24 * rows.length + 70,
  width: 1100,
  marginLeft: 200,
  marginBottom: 40,
  style: {fontSize: "12px"},
  x: {label: "Median claim-aligned partial r of the question (below zero supports the claim) →", domain: [-0.75, 0.45], grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: rows},
  marks: [
    band ? Plot.rectX([{x1: band[0], x2: band[1]}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "#c77c00", fillOpacity: 0.12}) : null,
    Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#5b6b78"}),
    Plot.ruleY(firstOfAxis, {stroke: "#d6dde5", strokeWidth: 1, dy: -12}),
    Plot.dot(neighbours.filter(d => d.exists && !d.isCurrent), {x: "median", y: "row", r: 5.5, fill: d => clusterColour[d.cluster], fillOpacity: 0.85, stroke: "none",
             title: d => `${d.row}\nmedian r_ca ${d.median.toFixed(3)}, range ${d.lo.toFixed(3)} to ${d.hi.toFixed(3)}, ${Math.round(100 * d.share_sig)}% significant`}),
    Plot.dot(neighbours.filter(d => d.exists && d.isCurrent), {x: "median", y: "row", r: 7, fill: "#c77c00", stroke: "none",
             title: d => `${d.row} (chosen)\nmedian r_ca ${d.median.toFixed(3)}`}),
    Plot.text(neighbours.filter(d => !d.exists), {x: -0.74, y: "row", text: () => "not in the universe", textAnchor: "start", fill: "#9aa8b3", fontSize: 11})
  ]
})
```

<p class="caption">One row for every option on every ring of the Level 1 dial, grouped by ring from the outside in. The orange dots are the six options under the index now. Each other dot is what the question's median answer becomes if that one ring is turned to that option and the other five are left as they are, in the ring's colour: blue for the three rings that name the variables, teal for the two that say whom the question is about, bronze for the estimator. The shaded band is where the middle 80% of the current question's own answers lie, across every combination of the Level 2 and Level 3 options. A dot outside the band means that turning that one ring moves the answer further than all the measurement and arithmetic decisions together can. Hover over a dot for that question's range and its share of significant answers.</p>

:::

<p class="caption">Every question the Level 1 dial can ask, the per-item rate counted with the count it rescales, each summarised by the median of its answers, with the chosen question marked in orange. Below zero supports the claim on every scale, because negative framings are reverse-coded and the sign convention for growth is flipped.</p>

:::

::: {.card title="How to read this page"}

<div class="small" style="max-width:75ch">
<p><b>The three dials</b> hold the fourteen choices, one ring each, and the option under the red index at twelve o'clock is the one chosen; click a segment to turn its ring. <b>The statement</b> is the test the course uses. Turn a ring of the Level 1 dial and the statement changes: a different question is being asked of the data, and two analysts who set it differently were not disagreeing about method. Turn a ring of the Level 2 dial and only the "measured as" words change; turn one of the Level 3 dial and nothing in the statement changes at all. The Level 1 rings come in three groups, from the outside in: the frame set, the scoring rule, the predictor and the adjustment set name the variables; the sample and the weight say whom the question is about; the estimator says how they are compared.</p>
<p><b>The answers to this question</b> shows all the ways the pre-computed grid answered the question the Level 1 dial fixes – every combination of the Level 2 and Level 3 options – ranked from most to least claim-supporting. Dark blue dots are significant at the five per cent level, grey ones are not, and the orange ring is the chosen specification. Colour the dots by one choice to find out which of its options sit where.</p>
<p><b>One ring at a time</b> shows what each alternative option on a Level 1 ring would do, holding the other five as they are: each dot is the median answer of that question, the orange dots are the chosen question, and the shaded band behind them is where the middle 80% of the current question's own answers lie. A dot outside the band means that turning that one ring moves the answer further than every Level 2 and Level 3 choice together.</p>
<p><b>All the questions</b> places the current question among every question the menu can ask, each summarised by its median answer; the per-item rate is counted with the count it rescales.</p>
<p>The <a href="spec-menu.qmd">specification menu</a> gives, for every choice, how much of the variation in results it carries and how often moving it alone crosses p = .05; the <a href="../companion/weighting.qmd">weighting</a> and <a href="../companion/missingness.qmd">missing-answers</a> pages take two of the Level 2 choices apart.</p>
</div>

:::
